issues.title: `validate.Email` accepts a leading/trailing hyphen in the last domain label
issues.body:
`validate.Email` is currently allowing domain names that start or end with a hyphen to bypass in certain cases such as “user@example.-com”, “user@example.com-”. We believe domain labels must not start or end with a hyphen (RFC 5321 §4.1.2), and Email already rejects this for the other labels, e.g. “user@ex-.com”

After some investigation, the cause is how `Email.DOMAIN_REGEX` matches the last domain label, which allows a hyphen to appear anywhere. To fix this, we can wrap that alternative in two lookarounds so the label can neither start nor end with a hyphen: `(?!-)` at the start and `(?<!-)` at the end. Django's `URLValidator` uses the same approach for its TLD regex. 

### Reproducible Tests
```python
from marshmallow import validate

email = validate.Email()
email("user@ex-.com")       # ValidationError, as expected
email("user@example.-com")  # passes
email("user@example.com-")  # passes
email("user@例え.-テスト")   # passes
```

### Proposed fixes
```diff
     r"(?:[A-Z" + _UNICODE_LETTERS + r"]{2,6}"
-    r"|[A-Z0-9" + _UNICODE_LETTERS + r"-]{2,})\Z"
+    r"|(?!-)[A-Z0-9" + _UNICODE_LETTERS + r"-]{2,}(?<!-))\Z"
```

### Version
marshmallow 4.3.1 (same on `dev` at 1c63bda), Python 3.12
